brief:
WHAT HAPPENED
- US President Trump announced a deal for Russian diesel, prompting criticism from Ukrainian President Zelensky.
- UK high street chemist Boots was sold to a Canadian billionaire family.
- Airlines raised alarms over an escalating cost crisis, according to the Financial Times.
- The White House blocked Microsoft from participating in a visa programme used to hire skilled foreign workers.
- Nvidia-backed data centre operator Firmus scrapped its initial public offering (IPO), citing market volatility and prevailing conditions.

WHY IT MATTERS
- An IPO (initial public offering)—the process where a private company sells shares to the public for the first time to raise money—being cancelled shows growing market caution over artificial intelligence business valuations.
- Visa restrictions on Microsoft signal heightened regulatory hurdles for major technology firms seeking global talent.
- Cost warnings from airlines highlight mounting financial strain on operating expenses across the transportation sector.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY
- International diplomatic responses to the US purchase of Russian diesel.
- Statements from Microsoft regarding restrictions on its foreign hiring programme.
- Updates from the airline industry detailing specific cost drivers behind the reported crisis.
- Further announcements regarding the transition and strategy for Boots under its new owners.

IN SIMPLE TERMS
Governments and corporations are confronting shifting economic pressures. The US entered a controversial deal for Russian fuel, while Microsoft faced new hiring limits on foreign staff. Meanwhile, an AI-related company pulled its planned stock market debut because of market turbulence, high street retailer Boots changed hands, and airlines warned of rising operational costs.
